court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Jaibai Rangnath Keskar And Another vs Gangubai Bhanudas Sakhare And Others

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Jaibai w/O Rangnath Keskar, Rajaram S/o Rangnath Keskar, Both R/o, Village Yelamba Ghat, Taluka and District Beed. ... APPELLANT (Orig. Plaintiffs)
parties.respondent_defendant: Gangubai W/o Bhanudas Sakhare, Died Through L.Rs., 1-A Narayan S/o Bhanudas Sakhare, 1-B Gorakhnath S/o Bhanudas Sakhare, 1-C Mathurabai W/o Saudegar Kadam, ... RESPONDENTS ( Orig. Defendants)

facts_of_case: Parties are Jaibai Rangnath Keskar and others vs Gangubai Bhanudas Sakhare and others. The case is about partition.

legal_principles.principle: In the event of a notional partition, the share of the deceased can be calculated immediately after death.
legal_principles.held: Rangnath could have been allotted by way of notional partition immediately on the date of death.

legal_principles.principle: The share of the deceased in a joint family property can be calculated based on the number of heirs.
legal_principles.held: The share of deceased Rangnath in the year 1961 in the joint family property could be only 1/3rd, the other 2/3rd share being that of son and wife of the deceased.

legal_principles.principle: The illegitimate child of a deceased person can only inherit the property that falls to their share.
legal_principles.held: In that event of the matter, the present respondent could inherit only to the property fallen to the share of deceased Rangnath at the time of his death along with the original defendants No.1 to 3 equally.

use_for_drafting: advising on Hindu Marriage and Succession Acts
